text: Let's turn Lesson 36's quarantine logic into a one-line decorator — expectations.

At dlt dot expect declares a named rule and a condition rows must satisfy. Compare this to Lesson 36's manual valid rows and quarantined rows split, built from two separate filter calls — here, the framework handles the actual enforcement.

There are three levels. Plain expect warns — keeps the row, just logs the violation. Expect or drop is Lesson 36's quarantine behavior, directly — bad rows never reach the table. Expect or fail is different again — one violation stops the entire pipeline run.

And this is genuinely less code for the same outcome. Lesson 36 needed two filter calls, a separate quarantine table write, and a separate metrics query. Here, three one-line decorators replace all of that.
And the pass-fail counts show up automatically in the pipeline UI — the same number Lesson 36 tracked by hand, now built into the platform. Next lesson: pipeline modes, triggered versus continuous.
